accepted.evidence: Turner 12646 explicitly records Pashai Darrai susuwā́ and Wegali sosəwá dry under śōṣu. Lehr Darrai sos- has the same s-s dry stem; its shorter lexical-stem notation is retained, without importing Turner’s adjectival ending.
Turner 10181 explicitly records Pashai muč- to flee and fall of a star under mucyátē escapes, alongside Ashkun muč- escape/flee. Lehr Darrai muc- flee matches the stem and meaning directly.

held.reason: Turner 9890 notes merger of mardati and *mr̥ndati branches; the relevant Pashai forms differ by dialect/nasalization from Lehr Darrai maṛ-.
Turner 4844 has northern split/tear stems, but Waigali is explicitly via Pashto and the immediate route into Darrai Pashai is not established.
Turner 8226 has exact northern squeeze stems, but no Pashai comparator and a nearby contact route remains possible.
